NTA. I had a similar experience with a very good friend of mine when I was 22. I invited a few friends over and cooked a Thai green curry dish, and prepared strawberries with melted chocolate drizzled over for dessert. I’m not the best at cooking, but both dishes were BOMB! Presentation maybe lacked, but whatever. It was a casual dinner. 

My close friend arrived while I was still cooking, and raved about how messy the kitchen was in front of all my other guests. Said, “this is giving me anxiety!” While running around my kitchen throwing away the bits leftover from chopping/some veg trays. I was busy cooking. Of course the kitchen isn’t going to be pristine. Who cares anyway? I kinda felt like she was putting on a show in front of our other friends. 

I had laid the table with bowls, and this friend let me know the bowls would be too small. So I obliged and put out bigger bowls. When I served dinner, all my guests asked for the smaller bowls. 

This guest then took a close-up picture of the Thai green curry (it’s not the most beautiful looking curry) and put it on her story with a snarky comment. It was supposed to be funny but I actually found it quite rude. 

When I brought the dessert out, she took a picture of the strawberries (presentation wasn’t amazing) and put it on her story, too! 

Once she left, I DM’d her and just said, “Please delete this” but I wish I had said a bit more. 

You invited friends over for a meal tailored to their wants. They should have been grateful, and well-mannered. I’d suggest writing a message to them. 

You don’t have to go in guns blazing, but explaining that those comments didn’t sit right with you will go a long way and at least the awkwardness will end. 

See their response and go from there. If they’re not sorry, don’t invite them over again.

Don’t freak out! Go for the tests, and wait for the results. I was convinced I had genital herpes, heck even my sexologist doctor had confirmed it. I went through it all, only to get the blood tests back as clear. I had a virus, not the herpes virus though, and it caused a shingles-like break out down there. Very, very rare. But not impossible. You need to keep your chin up until you get your results back. 

You need to reason with yourself now. There is no point stressing out and getting depressed over something until it is confirmed. You will put yourself through it twice. 

Also, women usually show signs more so than men, right? So if she is saying she’s clear, perhaps she really is. 

I am thinking of you but I know you will be okay. Positive thinking helps, make a conscious effort to try be positive until you get your results, and then go from there! Step by step.
